newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela tightens interbank currency trade.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela tightens interbank currency trade.

text.p: Venezuela's central bank on Monday introduced new limits on interbank foreign exchange trading, reclassifying a number of brokerages and institutions previously considered as "end clients."

According to a resolution obtained by Reuters, the central bank will now classify currency trading with any foreign bank, brokerage house and commercial bank not authorized as official currency traders as interbank trade. The names fill a five-page list.
The central bank established in 1996 that commercial banks must carry out 67 percent of all foreign currency trade with end clients and only 33 percent on the interbank market.

The measure sharply restricts the number of operations commercial banks will be able to classify as taking place with end clients and should reduce currency market volume and volatility, traders said.

"The reduced demand for dollars from end users, and the subsequent decline in the ability of foreign exchange traders to sell dollars in the interbank market, suggests a bias for bolivar strength," New York's IDEA said in a market comment.
"Late July weakness in the bolivar may well have been a concerted effort to get into dollars before foreign exchange market liquidity tightened," IDEA said.
The move to reclassify interbank currency operations coincided with the announcement that the central bank had raised reserve requirement for commercial banks by two percentage points to 17 percent.
The higher reserve requirement was needed to drain excess liquidity, which was expected to increase in coming weeks, traders said. The increase in the reserve requirement takes effect August 11.
